articles.title: SJAA Yosemite Star Party 2013
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted its annual Yosemite Star Party in 2013, bringing numerous telescopes to Glacier Point to share views of the night sky and the sun with park visitors as part of Yosemite's naturalist program. Despite an early-rising, bright moon and the nearby massive Rim Fire, SJAA members conducted successful public outreach, offering free admission and camping in exchange for their efforts. Coordinated by Jim Van Nuland, the event featured a variety of astronomical equipment and minimal direct impact from the wildfire, though it likely deterred general park visitors.

articles.title: Can Amateurs Image Any Detail Of The Cloud Bands On Uranus?
articles.summary: This article discusses the feasibility of amateur astronomers imaging cloud bands on Uranus, despite its small apparent size compared to other planets. It highlights successful attempts by amateurs like Ralf Vandebergh and Ed Grafton, showing visible detail and even moons. The piece also provides information about Uranus's opposition on October 3rd and how to locate it in the sky.

articles.title: Solar Observing at Houge Park
articles.summary: A well-attended solar observing event took place at Houge Park on Labor Day weekend, featuring four scope setups. Attendees observed superb H-Alpha flares, including quiescent prominences extending 40,000 miles and an active surge prominence reaching 80,000 miles, alongside 28 sunspots across three groups. The article also provides a detailed classification of solar prominences and promotes future monthly solar meetups at the park.

articles.title: Dark spots, bright spots
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for October, detailing various celestial events and targets. It highlights a multiple shadow transit of Jupiter, the fall Astronomy Day, and optimal viewing periods for planets like Uranus, Neptune, and Venus, as well as Comet C/2012 S1 ISON and sunspots. A significant portion explores the mysterious lunar albedo feature Reiner Gamma, discussing its appearance and speculative theories regarding its magnetic or impact-related origins.

articles.title: Quick STARt Program Experience
articles.summary: The author attended a 3-hour 'Quick STARt' class taught by Dave Ittner, covering fundamental aspects of amateur astronomy such as telescope types, light gathering, magnification, object location techniques (coordinates, sky hopping), and classifications of celestial bodies. The program included an outdoor viewing session, where stars and a galaxy were observed despite city lights and haze, and concluded with participants having the option to check out telescopes and library books. The author highly recommends this free, essential class for beginners in amateur astronomy, noting that SJAA membership is required.

articles.title: Rancho Canada del Oro 9/8 Report
articles.summary: This report details an astronomy observing session held at Rancho Canada del Oro on September 8th, featuring perfect weather, moonless skies, and a good turnout of both experienced observers and beginners. Highlights included clear views of the Milky Way, a bright blue-green fireball around 11:30 PM, and numerous meteor streaks throughout the night. The event was a success, fostering new connections among attendees.

articles.title: Expedition – Laguna Mountain
articles.summary: The article details an astronomical expedition to the remote Laguna Mountain in California, providing a comprehensive site report on the challenging journey, campground amenities, and the specific dark sky observing location. It describes the observing conditions, local light domes, and personal astronomical experiences, concluding that it is an excellent remote dark sky destination for individuals or small groups, particularly imagers. The author notes the land managers are open to suggestions for improvements to attract more visitors to the area.

articles.title: RASC 2014 Handbook
articles.summary: This article from the RASC 2014 Handbook details SJAA's acquisition of new handbooks for beginners and lists upcoming general meetings, including a 'Show & Tell' and a talk on the Sun. It also provides updates on club programs, noting that the Quick STARt program is at capacity and the Advanced Loaner Telescope Program needs more mounts while anticipating the addition of a 17-inch custom Dobsonian.

articles.title: SJAA Library Needs Help
articles.summary: The article highlights the stagnation of the SJAA Library program, with a call for volunteers passionate about astronomy and books to manage it. It also details key discussions from the SJAA's September Board Meeting, including the approval of the 2014 calendar, the formation of a member recognition committee, a new procedure for an 'Astronomy Technology Today' discount, and the approval of terms and conditions for lending Jack Zeider's 17" Dobsonian telescope.

articles.title: School Star Party Program
articles.summary: The article provides an update on the School Star Party Program, detailing completed events for the 2013-14 school year up to September 17, 2013, including statistics on sky conditions and success rates. It also lists scheduled events from September to May, indicating the number of firm and working dates. Additionally, a brief report on the Fix-It Program mentions a slow session over Labor Day weekend with some basic work done on club QuickSTARt scopes.
